messages:
oliver (Acme): Hey team — our nightly bulk ingest (runs from a k8s job behind a NATed egress) started seeing widespread 429s at 02:03 UTC. We use an API key in X-API-Key and also send an Authorization: Bearer header for fallback. Happening since last deploy.

sophia (Support): thanks @oliver, can you paste an example request header (sanitized) + the NAT egress IP?

oliver (Acme): sure — IP: 34.78.192.11
Headers:
  X-API-Key: redacted-abc
  Authorization: Bearer redacted-jwt
  Content-Type: application/json

Also attaching our k8s job window: runs every 5m for 30m at 02:00-02:30 local.

miguel (SRE): quick check: logs show a lot of "quota_exceeded" routed to org-level limit for acme-org, but the API key id isn't being shown in the auth log lines. Example from auth log around 1763001310:
  auth_result=ip_scoped quota_namespace=org:acme-org quota_id=org-monthly-2M api_key_id=null request_ip=34.78.192.11 path=/v1/generate

sophia (Support): that is odd — if both X-API-Key and Authorization present we should pick API key precedence and attribute to project key scope. @miguel can you grep for the request headers for that trace id?

miguel (SRE): pulled the raw header dump for trace=trc-87921:
  headers_order:["Host","X-Forwarded-For","X-API-Key","User-Agent","Authorization","Content-Type"]
Raw header blob shows X-API-Key present but downstream auth parser returned api_key=null. Hypothesis: our internal auth middleware reads headers stream-first and uses first auth token it recognizes; some older edge-case code path treats Authorization after X-API-Key as "secondary" and drops it if the token fails verification, falling back to IP-based attribution.

oliver (Acme): so because of header order our API key isn't being applied and traffic gets attributed to org IP bucket? that would explain the 429s — org monthly cap exhausted.

miguel (SRE): yes looks like that. Also saw repeated 401 attempts against the API key validator (timing aligns). If the X-API-Key verification fails transiently (timeout to key service), middleware falls back to trying IP-based mapping rather than waiting for the key verification to finish.

sophia (Support): short-term mitigation options:
  1) support-ops-bot can apply a temporary org quota bump to prevent customer outage (safest quick fix).
  2) client can remove the redundant Authorization header from the request so only X-API-Key is present.
  3) recommend switching to sending only Authorization: Bearer if you want JWT routing (but pick one).

support-ops-bot: temporary quota bump applied: org acme-org +5M tokens for 24h by request 4332. :white_check_mark:

oliver (Acme): appreciate that, we'll patch our proxy to strip the Authorization header while we diagnose. Any long-term fix on your side?

miguel (SRE): filed infra ticket INFRA-1278 (auth-precedence: ensure atomic auth resolution and do not fall back to IP attribution on transient key validation failures). Proposed change: block attribution until key validator returns definitive result and keep request in pending auth state for up to 300ms before fallback.

sophia (Support): also adding doc note: "If you send multiple auth methods, ensure the one you expect is validated first — avoid simultaneous X-API-Key + Authorization to prevent ambiguous attribution." We'll link when updated.

oliver (Acme): repro steps we used (for your triage):
  curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'X-API-Key: redacted-abc' 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer redacted-jwt' 
    -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
  Observed 429 with body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","scope":"org"}

miguel (SRE): verified repro by replaying request with header order swapped (Authorization first, X-API-Key second) — gets attributed correctly to key scope. When X-API-Key appears before Authorization and our key validator responded with a 504 for that trace, it fell back to IP scope.

sophia (Support): next steps:
  - oliver: patch proxy to strip Authorization (ETA today) and confirm no more 429s.
  - support: keep temporary quota bump for 24h, will extend if patch needs more time.
  - infra: INFRA-1278 assigned to miguel, target short-term fix and a long-term robust auth state machine.
  - docs: add guidance about header collisions and recommend single auth header.

oliver (Acme): proxy patch deployed, removed Authorization header at ingress. Running now — will report back in 10m. :pray:

miguel (SRE): I've added correlation logs and an alert for any future traces where api_key_id==null but X-API-Key header present; will escalate if seen.

oliver (Acme): after patch — ingestion resumed, no 429s in the last 20m. Thanks for quick help! :raised_hands:

sophia (Support): great to hear. I'll close the ticket after INFRA-1278 is scheduled and docs updated. Leaving record here for future: header-order + transient validator failures -> accidental IP/org attribution -> quota exhaustion.

miguel (SRE): INFRA-1278: backlog -> p1 mitigation: change auth middleware to prefer definitive verification, instrument metrics for key validation latency.

sophia (Support): resolved for now. Follow-ups: update public FAQ and include a short note in onboarding about not sending multiple auth headers.

oliver (Acme): thanks everyone.
_meta: generated for dataset: support thread about auth scoping edge-case; contains sanitized headers and internal references
